speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens exactly when you wake up frightened? Do you have any dreams, or does it feel like someone is chasing you?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you or anyone in the house hear strange sounds, smells, or see figures in your room at night, or do you simply feel afraid without a specific cause? REQUEST TEST: Sleep_Studies; REQUEST IMAGES: Polysomnography_report.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sleep Diary Findings indicate disturbances occurring 1-2 times per week correlating with described episodes. Polysomnography Findings: Not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination. NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors) in an 8-year-old female.

The diagnosis of pyelonephritis mentioned by your previous doctor does not match your symptoms of waking up frightened without confusion, which is characteristic of sleep terrors rather than a kidney infection. Although a kidney infection can cause fatigue, it typically presents with fever, flank pain, and burning during urination, none of which you described. We will proceed with monitoring sleep hygiene and safety measures, as the sleep study report you requested will likely be normal. Do you have any history of bedwetting or other sleepwalking behaviors during these episodes?
